vocab.title: Match each term to its meaning
defs: a
the price for coffee that is delivered now
b
coffee beans that are not roasted yet
c
the amount of water in the beans
d
a person or company that connects buyers and sellers
e
a professional tasting that gives a coffee a score
f
high-quality coffee with a score of eighty or more
g
where coffee is bought and sold for a future date
h
a problem in a bean, like a black or broken bean
i
to protect yourself against a big change in price
j
a group of bags of the same coffee, sold together
k
the amount added to or taken from the futures price
l
to decide the final price of a contract

listenings.text: Every morning, the first thing that a coffee trader checks is the futures market in New York. The futures price is the base price for arabica coffee around the world, and it changes every minute. But nobody pays only the futures price. The real price of a lot is the futures price plus a differential, which depends on the quality, the origin and the market. Then there is the spot price, which is the price for coffee that you can deliver now. Why is all this important? Because prices can go up or down very fast. A frost in Brazil can change everything in one night. That is why companies hedge. A roaster that buys coffee for next year can fix part of the price today, so a big change in the market does not destroy its budget. My advice for new traders is simple: learn the words first. If you understand the futures, the differential and the hedge, you understand the business.

I have been working as a coffee taster in Santos for twelve years. My day starts at seven, when the samples that arrived the day before are ready. First, I look at the green coffee. I count the defects, the black and broken beans that lower the quality. Then I check the moisture content, because coffee that is too wet can get mold during the trip. After that, we roast a small amount and do the cupping. We smell the coffee, and then we taste it with a spoon, very loudly. Every coffee gets a score. A lot that gets eighty points or more is specialty coffee, and the buyers who look for specialty pay a much better price. The hardest part of my job is to be consistent. The score that I give on Monday must be the same score that I would give on Friday.

extra_audio.text: First, the samples of green coffee arrive at the lab. Then the taster counts the defects and checks the moisture content. After that, the team does the cupping and gives the lot a score. A lot that scores eighty points or more is sold as specialty coffee. The price is the futures price plus a differential. Finally, the buyer fixes the price before the shipment.
